encounters.title: Underhall of the Hollow Feast
encounters.summary: Beneath sixty-three carved doors, Judith joins signed gratitude, household carriers, captive voices, and three old betrayals into one invitation.
encounters.opening_view: Below Blackbriar Hall, sixty-three freestanding doors show household hearths as they are tonight. Blackthorn tokens glow on mantels; paper-thin thresholds wait for signatures; other doors remain dark. Odo Vane fits Mercy Book leaves around a four-sided lectern. Captain Cleft presses warm iron echoes into the root table. Living captives are strapped beneath silver mouthpieces as the wagon hoist lowers another covered shape. Judith sits at a table laid for four, with three empty chairs behind her. One household door swings inward. A frightened woman asks who has entered her home.
encounters.content:
## Situation

Begin by inventorying what actually reached the chamber: Mercy Book pages and index, warm token sockets, living controlled voices, pit-dead or white roots, Judith, her lieutenants, and each surviving pact. Set the feast stage from elapsed time and prior responses. A missing body, page, carrier, witness, or commander stays missing; the reference library does not preload the finale.

Four struggles proceed at once; one ritual roll or Judith's remaining endurance cannot settle them together:

- Judith's body, position, and ability to issue commands;
- the **common welcome**, which needs at least two of its three components to remain joined;
- the captives, prisoners, and households exposed through the chamber; and
- the patrons whose pacts still possess a material claim.

Earlier work must be visible. Revoked doors face outward. Returned names leave silent choir bays. Honest burials take white roots from the table. An opened refuge makes copied thresholds swing away from the Guest. Seized records, controlled routes, divided lieutenants, and protected witnesses change who can act before the first weapon is raised.
## Entering the Underhall

The main stair descends from Judith's study. The service tunnel enters a wagon gallery above the household doors. Reflected routes can reach the choir bays while the Child pact remains intact. A hearth crossing can emerge through a corresponding household door while the Guest remains intact and that household has not revoked.

Forcing the inner stair advances the feast one stage but creates a permanent route. Entering through a household door exposes that household until its carrier is removed or the door is turned outward. Following the wagon gives access to the prisoners before the main defenders can fully redeploy.

## The chamber

### Wagon gallery

The service tunnel ends on a stone gallery with room for two wagons. Prisoners, Mercy Book packets, spare tokens, and bodies from the White Pits are received here. Two hoists descend to the choir bays and central table.

Controlling the gallery prevents new captives, guards, or records from reaching the rite. It does not by itself stop components already in place.

### Sixty-three household doors

The doors stand in seven rows of nine; only doors with a surviving signature, token, stolen ash, or another actual household carrier can connect. Through a connected door lies the matching hearth as it currently exists, not an illusion of an ideal home.

- A fully marked and unrevoked household shows a clear room and warm token.
- A signed but tokenless household shows a paper-thin doorway that cannot carry a body until a token is placed.
- A privately revoked household smokes and gives no stable view.
- A publicly revoked household faces outward and cannot be counted in the common welcome.
- A household whose carriers were destroyed carelessly may show uncontrolled fire, a false reflection, or a sick resident depending on the channel disturbed.

A person at a doorway can speak to the household, move a small object, or cross if the Guest and matching token permit. This creates opportunities for warning and revocation as well as danger.

### Mercy lectern

The Mercy Book rests on a four-sided lectern. The master index joins separated pages carried by Corin and other servants. Odo reads household names and obligations from one side; Judith signs acceptance from another.

The book can be neutralized in several materially different ways:

- remove it from the lectern and keep the master index apart from the pages;
- cut or tear out accurately identified household entries after their residents revoke;
- correct the entries under independent witness through the petition-hall speaking tube or honest bell;
- soak or otherwise render the signatures unusable after preserving necessary evidence;
- destroy the book after removing stolen names and evidence needed for the pact operations.

Burning it while the Guest remains intact sends signed ash into the household hearths and strengthens that component for one stage. Smashing it without separating written child names leaves those names available to the Child Behind Glass.

### Token table

A blackthorn root spreads across a low table and ends in sixty-three iron sockets. Forty-seven hold warm token echoes. Eleven hold empty paper rings for signed households. Five are cold.

The token component remains operational while the root can match enough actual hearth carriers to the Mercy Book. It can be neutralized by severing the central root after the Guest pact is broken, by removing and separately containing the warm sockets, or by making the relevant household doors face outward through witnessed revocation.

Cutting the root while the Guest remains intact sends inward flame toward every connected hearth. Protection requires opened doors, cooled sockets, guarded households, or acceptance of the burn. Removing sockets one by one is slower but does not spread the fire.

### Choir bays

Seven narrow bays surround the table. Each is marked for one stolen name: Nell Sedge, Amey Fen, Jo Rusk, Lark Merrow, Perrin Mett, Sella Darr, and Corin Pike. Judith needs at least four controlled voices from living captives speaking at once for the captive-choir component to function. A vessel, copied strip, borrowed recording, commanded servant, or remote voice may help control or imitate a child, but none counts as that child's physical voice in a bay.

A captive whose name has been returned cannot be used even if physically present. A bay can also be disabled by freeing its captive, removing the written-name strip, covering the silver mouthpiece, or substituting a free witness who openly refuses the welcome. Judith can move a controlled child between bays, but she cannot make one child count as two.

Captives are not helpless ritual objects. They can interrupt rhythm, exchange names, bite through wax, relay instructions through doors, and choose whether to remain long enough to help other households revoke. Do not require them to risk themselves merely because doing so is tactically useful.

### Dead table

Thirty-one white place settings correspond to the founding pit-dead. Five smaller settings correspond to the renewal trench. If the Worm remains intact, abandoned bodies or white roots answer the supper bell and carry Judith's wounds.

Each honestly identified founding body removes one setting from Judith's protection. Each lifted body leaves a chair that cannot rise. Honest final disposition of all thirty-one breaks the Worm's claim. The later five no longer strengthen the founding pact, but recovering them prevents Judith from using their bodies as immediate servants and provides living families with evidence.

The honest bell can be sounded here if it has been brought from the chapel or mounted at the pits. Its sound makes every wound transfer visible and causes the dead to answer with their own names rather than Judith's feast response.

### Three patron chairs

The chairs stand behind Judith.

- The Guest's chair is charred beneath intact varnish.
- The Worm's chair is white and damp without being cold.
- The Child's chair reflects a seated child who is never present in the room.

Completed pact work changes the chairs permanently. Weakened work exposes remaining obligations. A severed pact splits its chair and prevents that patron's full manifestation. Two broken chairs make Judith bodily mortal. Three broken chairs leave the feast without an inheriting patron even if household claims remain.

### Judith's place

Judith sits at the fourth side of the table with the contingency matrix beneath her plate. Her position joins command of the components but is not itself a component. Killing, displacing, binding, or forcing her from the place stops her personal coordination. The Court can continue if two feast components and at least one pact remain.

## The three feast components

The **common welcome** exists while at least two of these three components remain operational:

1. **Mercy Book:** written hosts and accepted obligations joined by the master index.
2. **Token network:** physical household carriers connected through the token table and ash gallery.
3. **Captive choir:** at least four controlled stolen-name voices speaking the welcome.

Neutralizing any one weakens and delays the rite. Neutralizing any two collapses the valley-wide welcome into isolated household claims. Those remaining claims can still endanger individual homes until revoked, but the Court can no longer enter the vale as one invited household.

Reveal this rule through Judith's contingency matrix, the chamber's behavior, or prior clues—not as a menu of endings. Available operations come from the people, evidence, tools, and routes actually secured.

## Feast stages

Begin at the stage justified by elapsed time and prior Judith responses. Advance when Judith completes an action, prolonged work goes unopposed, or a failed operation gives one component control. A round ending by itself changes nothing.

### Stage 1: Places laid

Odo joins the Mercy Book pages. Tokens warm in their sockets. Captives are placed in the bays. Records and people remain interceptable until the components are physically joined.

### Stage 2: Households named

Odo reads the sixty-three household names. Connected doors clarify. Publicly revoked households turn outward. Correcting an entry through witness or bell removes it from the common count and may cause Odo to lose his place.

### Stage 3: Gifts answered

Cleft, Harl if still loyal, or household servants recite what each household accepted. The token table sends heat through matching hearths. Removing sockets, opening doors, or distributing warnings creates immediate local choices.

### Stage 4: Children speak

The controlled voices answer for the vale. Judith needs four. Returned names speak freely, not in unison. A captive's clear refusal can guide a household through a doorway but does not substitute for rescuing or protecting that child.

### Stage 5: The dead attend

The Worm's bell sounds. White settings rise, injuries leave Judith's body, and stored illness moves toward the doors. The honest bell, named bodies, or a severed Worm prevent or reduce this response visibly.

### Stage 6: Betrayed welcome closes

The Guest turns connected doors inward and tries to bar exit from each represented home. Correctly opened refuge doors force copies outward; restored names let the refuge dead state what Judith did; the burned living ledger leaves the Guest without a host claim.

### Stage 7: Common invitation

If at least two feast components and at least one pact remain, the doors join into one threshold. Manifestations enter according to surviving pacts. Judith claims mastery or, if dead, becomes the first thing the Court consumes.

### Stage 8: Midnight possession

If the common welcome remains and no one contests control, the surviving patrons establish continuing access. This is not an automatic campaign end. Publicly revoked households remain outside, rescued names resist command, severed patrons are absent, and witnesses retain evidence. Record exactly what the Court gained rather than declaring the whole vale simply lost.

## Judith's capabilities by pact state

Judith normally takes one decisive action through one intact channel and one ordinary action through a servant, weapon, position, or command. Do not let three patrons become unlimited action economy.

### Guest in Ash

**Intact:** Judith crosses connected hearths, denies a threshold, turns one domestic flame inward, or hides a movement in soot.

**Doors opened:** Threshold effects leave visible soot and require a physical door to move. She cannot silently imprison someone behind a claimed threshold.

**Names restored:** Refuge dead can contradict her, copied doors repeat their names, and her soot concealment leaves a speaking trail.

**Severed:** Hearth crossing, inward fire, and threshold denial end. Ordinary fire and doors remain.

### Worm in White

**Intact:** Judith transfers one significant wound or illness into a known pit body, animates abandoned remains, or sends stored sickness through a prepared line.

**Honest bell sounded:** Transfers become visible white threads and can be intercepted. The dead can answer with their own gestures or names.

**Bodies identified or lifted:** Judith has fewer valid recipients. Use the actual remaining bodies; do not invent replacements.

**Severed:** Wounds remain on Judith, abandoned bodies fall, transferred illness stops moving, and pact rot ends.

### Child Behind Glass

**Intact:** Judith commands one person through a controlled written name, borrows a known voice, opens one reflected route, or creates one false familiar figure.

**Individual names returned:** That person cannot be commanded, imitated, or used to open a route. Their bay fails.

**Mirrors covered or tested:** The affected route or false figure ends even while other names remain controlled.

**Severed:** Borrowed voices, name commands, false recognition, and reflected routes end. Mirrors become ordinary.

### Bodily protection

- With all three pacts intact, lethal harm can be distributed among ash, dead flesh, and stolen reflection. Judith can be driven off or restrained only by controlling the carriers she would use.
- With one pact severed, she loses that defense and power family but can still divert fatal harm through the other two.
- With two pacts severed, Judith is bodily mortal. She bleeds, cannot leave by a lost channel, and remains where physical restraint places her.
- With all three severed, she is an exceptionally prepared but ordinary mortal practitioner with servants, weapons, poisons, records, and no supernatural patron defense.

## Judith's conduct in the finale

Judith remains socially exact under pressure. She names practical costs, not cosmic abstractions. She offers a cure that would move illness into Eda, a child's release in exchange for another household page, or safe departure while the village remains claimed. She never offers restitution, shared custody, or surrender of a claim. Every concession substitutes a new victim or preserves her title to the old one.

When a component fails, she does not shriek or become incoherent. She changes ownership strategy.

- If the Mercy Book fails, she tries to preserve tokens and force the children to name individual hosts.
- If the token network fails, she moves to signed pages and reflected access through named residents.
- If the choir fails, she uses Odo, Harl, or a commanded household representative as witnesses, but those voices cannot restore the choir component.
- If a pact severs, she abandons that patron's chair and exploits the others.
- If two pacts sever, she seeks a physical exit, hostage, or negotiated surrender because she knows she can now be killed.
- If all three sever, she may attempt to burn evidence, kill a particular witness, or flee through an ordinary route. She does not gain a hidden fourth patron.

Judith prefers punishments that make someone participate: ordering Cleft to put a child in a parent's doorway, making Odo read his own prepared accusation, or offering a household medicine only if it speaks the welcome. Keep the target reachable and the choice contestable.

## Lieutenants and divided loyalties

### Odo Vane

Odo controls the Mercy lectern, seals, and phrases by which injury becomes procedure. He calls children dependents and murder disposition. Exposure makes him offer one record or captive in exchange for his daughter's place and his own office. He will falsify surrender unless separated from ink, knife, and seal.

### Varro Cleft

Cleft holds the token table and armed defenders. He treats each open household door as leverage against a person elsewhere and orders ordinary guards to stand where marked guards can be spent. Loss of command, isolation from the table, or physical defeat ends his role. Conscience does not.

### Garran Pike

If loyal and present, Garran controls the wagon gallery and the only orderly retreat. If broken, he can turn the road, cut reinforcement, or bring Olla under the bell. His aid changes movement and timing, not his culpability.

### Sister Harl

Harl's state follows Saint Mercy House. Loyal, she counts choir bays and calls restraint continuity of care. Broken with Judith, she knows every buckle and can hold one route. Absent, Tib Wale or Merrit Coil performs the work badly and with less resident trust.

### Ordinary staff and guards

They do not share one courage or one excuse. Resolve each by prior commitment, dependent, payment, witnessed pact effect, and whether someone has offered a survivable refusal. Some flee. Some free captives. Some continue for wages after command is gone.

## Patron manifestations

Manifest only patrons whose pacts still possess a substantial claim. Each speaks and acts through the obligation Judith inverted.

### The Guest in Ash

The Guest appears as hands closing doors from the household side and as an occupied emptiness in every offered chair. Its speech is impeccable invitation: “May I keep the door you asked me to close?” “Will you leave these people outside so that your own may be safe?” It tries to turn rescue into trespass and refuge into title. Open doors, restored refuge names, freely offered hearths, and the burned ledger answer it in the only language it honors.

### The Worm in White

The Worm arrives as damp lime beneath plates, white roots in abandoned flesh, and wounds entering the wrong body. It counts rather than argues: bodies unnamed, witnesses absent, dispositions unfinished. Its bargains offer speed, stillness, and exact identifications in exchange for one person left without a final account. Names, careful lifting, the honest bell, and completed burial remove one item at a time from its tally.

### The Child Behind Glass

The Child appears in each uncovered surface as the person the viewer most expects to trust. It speaks in borrowed cadences and asks apparently small questions: “Which name should I keep when you leave?” “May I answer as your mother once?” “Would you know the prisoner if I wore the face?” It seeks recognition, repetition, and permission to stand for someone absent. Returned names, covered surfaces, unborrowed reflections, and free refusal leave it visible but handleless.

A manifestation is not a second all-purpose villain. The Guest closes, the Worm transfers and tallies, and the Child substitutes. Press the old violation; do not invent unrelated powers.

## Stopping the feast

The feast is stopped cleanly when the common welcome collapses and no intact patron can inherit Judith's coordinating claim. This can occur through many sequences of actual play.

- Earlier household revocations may have turned enough doors outward that the token component is easy to dismantle.
- A Mercy House rescue may already have removed four choir voices.
- Captured pages, Corin's key, and public witnesses may neutralize the Mercy Book quickly.
- Severed pact chairs may make direct confrontation with Judith and the manifestations tractable.
- Control of the wagon gallery may prevent moved captives or replacement records from arriving.
- A direct assault may kill Judith first, leaving the surviving components to be stopped while the Court tries to inherit them.

Keep these consequences behind the screen until action exposes them. Apply the component and pact rules to what actually happens.

## If Judith falls

Judith can be killed while pacts remain once two have been severed, or if every surviving recipient of her distributed harm is physically controlled. If Judith is killed or rendered unconscious, remove her personal coordination and ordinary actions immediately.

- If two or three feast components remain and at least one pact survives, the patron chairs turn toward the Mercy Book and the rite continues.
- If fewer than two components remain, the common welcome collapses even if a patron survives.
- If all three pacts are severed, no patron can inherit her place. Remaining household carriers are dangerous local objects, not a valley-wide invitation.
- Judith's body may still contain evidence: written names under the tongue, ash in old burns, white lime beneath healed scars, and silver behind one eye. Handle those carriers rather than assuming death purifies them.

Judith may be killed, captured, abandoned to the patrons, or driven into flight. Record the result and every obligation that remains.

## Authority after the confrontation

The commission may continue Mara's stay, preserve records, protect rescued people, and detain Judith or an officer caught attacking witnesses, captives, or evidence. It may not award Blackbriar Hall, appoint a permanent government, compel a child to testify, settle every confiscated title, or pronounce final judgment on collaborators.

A temporary local council is legitimate only if named household, parish, care, and civil representatives accept the work publicly, its powers are limited to food, refuge, medical care, evidence custody, immediate safety, and contact with outside authorities, and its end condition is stated. If no such coalition forms, the ending must name the narrower custodians who actually hold each person, store, record, and dangerous carrier.

## Failure-forward outcomes

Failure in the Underhall produces a specific claim, loss, or rescue problem.

- One feast component becomes fully active while another remains contestable.
- A patron manifests through a subset of household doors rather than the whole vale.
- Judith escapes through a surviving hearth, road, or mirror and leaves evidence behind.
- Odo carries a page packet into the village, creating a pursuit and local household danger.
- Cleft takes one choir captive to the wagon gallery while other bays are freed.
- Stored illness enters three named connected households, which can be isolated and treated.
- The common welcome collapses, but several private household claims remain unrepealed.
- Judith dies before the pact sites are repaired, leaving patron manifestations to be contained.

Avoid replacing a mixed result with “the ritual succeeds” or “the ritual fails.” State exactly which components, pacts, people, doors, and channels remain.

## Final record

At the end of the confrontation, record:

- Judith alive, captured, dead, escaped, or taken by a patron;
- Odo, Cleft, Garran, Harl, and principal staff states;
- Guest, Worm, and Child pacts intact, weakened, or severed;
- Mercy Book operational, neutralized, preserved, corrected, or destroyed;
- token network operational, fragmented, contained, or severed;
- each of the seven choir bays and name states;
- household doors connected, privately revoked, publicly turned outward, or locally endangered;
- Mara, Tomas, Nell, other captives, Eda Lorn, and pit-dead outcomes;
- patron manifestations remaining in the vale;
- evidence and relief stores preserved;
- immediate medical, burial, refuge, food, and legal needs;
- and who has authority to undertake those tasks.

A complete victory exposes and ends Judith's system without making fifteen years of harm vanish at midnight. A partial victory may save most people while leaving local claims, a fugitive witch, an intact patron, or contested institutions for the aftermath. The chamber reflects every person, record, route, and obligation preserved earlier.

## Arriving with partial knowledge

The Underhall remains physically legible after a direct assault.

- The Mercy Book, token table, and choir bays visibly perform different parts of the invitation. Reachable machinery may be disrupted, seized, covered, freed, disconnected, or destroyed without first checking a revelation box.
- The first time Judith displaces a wound, crosses an inward-turning door, or commands a stolen name, show the actual recipient, carrier, and trace. This reveals an immediate tactical problem and may point toward a remote site.
- A patron chair or manifestation can demonstrate the violated obligation it still uses. It does not complete the refuge opening, pit burial, or name-return sequence elsewhere.
- A missing counter-rite remains missing. Do not convert broad knowledge that Judith has three pacts into the exact material steps for all three severances.
- Direct attackers can still collapse the common welcome by neutralizing two feast components, free captives, divide lieutenants, preserve evidence, force Judith through a traceable exit, or contain a local manifestation.

Partial information changes preparation and available remedies, not permission to act. State what is visible, what each action changes, and which obligations remain elsewhere.

Odo's command of the Mercy lectern, seals, and accusation language explains one feast role without fixing his allegiance or control.
Cleft's force and custody methods explain the restraint bays and guard threat without establishing captives, numbers, or survival.
Harl's resident knowledge and transfer competence explain the choir bays and evacuation burdens without deciding whether she serves or resists Judith.
His page-number key and stolen name affect the Mercy leaves and one choir bay without deciding his presence.
The wagon gallery and route knowledge make him a possible lieutenant whose allegiance remains unresolved.
Its records, residents, transfer work, and captive system can supply or deprive the feast only through prior play.
The stair, undercroft, service tunnel, and household government above define the chamber’s ordinary access.
Opened doors and restored names permanently alter the Guest’s thresholds and patron chair.
Identified and honestly disposed bodies remove settings and wound-transfer protection from the table.
Threshold, burial, naming, and bell procedures remain usable below only if actually brought and supported.
Returned names silence bays and close reflected routes without assuming any captive’s body is safe.
The wagon gallery receives the people, pages, bodies, and guards that survive the road contest.
The doors, lectern, token table, bays, dead settings, chairs, and Judith’s place form the final operating surface.
Cleft’s force, marked bodies, and ordinary staff remain separate actors rather than one automatic defense.
At least two joined components and one surviving patron are required for the common invitation to continue.
Its chair, thresholds, and household fire reflect the exact refuge work completed before arrival.
Its chair, white settings, bodies, and wound transfers reflect the burial work actually completed.
Its chair, choir control, mirrors, and borrowed voices reflect names actually restored or still held.
The lectern and master index join written hosts only while pages and signatures remain materially usable.
The socket table depends on real household carriers and revocations rather than a symbolic count.
If present and usable, its sound exposes transfers and permits honest names to answer in the chamber.
Vessels can support control or reflected access but cannot substitute for four living captive voices.

revelations.title: Mara hid the case against Judith at Sedge Croft
revelations.description: Seven prosecution packets, Nell's map, the planted gift, and the stolen hearth ash show how Judith selected victims and how Nell was taken.

revelations.title: Saint Mercy House keeps Judith's stolen children
revelations.description: Behind the useful charity are hidden captives, seven name vessels, the Mercy Book, and patients carrying illnesses Judith moved out of favored bodies.

revelations.title: Blackbriar Hall is the working center of Judith's rule
revelations.description: The estate joins petitioners and relief stores to confiscation records, the ash gallery, pact ledgers, commanded retainers, prisoner routes, and the stair below.

revelations.title: Betrayed shelter feeds the Guest in Ash
revelations.description: Judith's power over hearths and thresholds begins in the granary where she barred nineteen workers inside the shelter they had repaired for her.

revelations.title: Denied burial feeds the Worm in White
revelations.description: Thirty-one pox dead lie erased in orchard quicklime, carrying Judith's transferred sickness, animated flesh, rot, and diverted wounds.

revelations.title: The open chapel keeps the rites Judith fears
revelations.description: Its rolls, broken honest bell, and surviving offices show how to withdraw welcome, witness denied burial, and return a stolen name without claiming its owner.

revelations.title: Judith delivers stolen names at Moonless Mere
revelations.description: Silvered vessels descend into the pool, where the Child Behind Glass turns names into handles for dreams, voices, recognition, command, and reflected travel.

revelations.title: Crow Wood is Judith's road for messages and captives
revelations.description: Crows, ash packets, written names, Garran Pike's wagon, the Glass Nurse, and the hall service tunnel exchange cargo along paths redirected by carried marks.

revelations.title: The Hollow Feast opens beneath Blackbriar Hall
revelations.description: At midnight the Underhall can join every household door that still carries a valid claim when at least two of the Mercy Book, token network, and four-voice captive choir remain active.

revelations.title: Judith made the witches she condemned
revelations.description: She planted evidence, moved illness, prepared confessions, removed dependents, and used ordinary officers to turn each chosen household's fear into another claim of protection.

revelations.title: Judith bought her power three times
revelations.description: She knowingly renewed bargains with the Guest in Ash, the Worm in White, and the Child Behind Glass. No curse, coercion, or hidden necessity compelled her.

revelations.title: Every mercy token is a door-key
revelations.description: A marked gift joined to a gratitude signature lets Judith claim the household's threshold and, during the feast, present that claim to her patrons.

revelations.title: Judith's omniscience has carriers
revelations.description: Tokens, copied names, stolen ash, marked servants, mirrors, crows, and written messages move information and force through a network that can be mapped, intercepted, and cut.

revelations.title: Open the refuge and burn the lie
revelations.description: Open the barred doors without welcoming the Guest, restore the nineteen betrayed names, and burn Judith's living false ledger in a hearth freely offered by one she betrayed.

revelations.title: Name, lift, and bury the stolen dead
revelations.description: Identify the founding dead, extract them safely from quicklime, and bury or burn each beneath an honest bell that records the body, the place, and the denial.

revelations.title: Return each name before breaking its vessel
revelations.description: The owner or a free witness must speak the name into an unborrowed reflection; only then can the matching silvered vessel be shattered without further injury.

revelations.title: Two broken pacts make Judith mortal
revelations.description: Each patron catches a different defeat. With two pacts severed, harm remains on Judith's body; with all three severed, the Court cannot cleanly inherit her place.

revelations.title: Break two feast components to end the common welcome
revelations.description: The rite needs the Mercy Book, marked household tokens, and at least four controlled stolen-name voices. Remove any two; Judith's death by itself leaves the invitation running.

clues.title: Mara names seven packets beneath the blue board
clues.description: Between smoke-coughs Mara names the seven households she compared and tells Tomas which workroom board is stained with birthing blue. Judith's people came for her before she could carry the packets to the canon.
clues.discovery: Keep Mara conscious long enough to give the household names, or hear Tomas repeat the hiding instruction exactly.

clues.title: Nell's reflection asks for the loose board
clues.description: One hanging mirror shows Nell at Saint Mercy House repeating that her mother's comparison packets are beneath the loose board in the Sedge workroom.
clues.discovery: Identify Nell’s reflection and listen before the Child Behind Glass notices the attention.

clues.title: Order to strip the Sedge house
clues.description: A Blackbriar memorandum directs Quill to remove ‘the family comparisons’ before Canon Ysra's agents arrive and orders Odo to advance Mara's burning to first light, before the customary answer-night.
clues.discovery: Read Judith’s desk orders or intercept a servant carrying them.

clues.title: Mara counts missing children in the white-house windows
clues.description: Mara names Nell's blackthorn gift, the hour her shadow bent into the hearth, and three earlier children seen behind Saint Mercy House glass after their families were told they had gone away.
clues.discovery: Let Mara state the sequence before the crowd, or take her testimony under protection after the stay.

clues.title: Nell's map of the long white house
clues.description: The map beneath Nell’s bed shows the Mercy House dormitory, hanging mirrors, and the laundry drain.
clues.discovery: Search Nell’s room or ask Tomas where his sister hid drawings.

clues.title: Night transfers from the Hall
clues.description: A service schedule records named children moved between Mercy House and Blackbriar Hall after public visiting hours.
clues.discovery: Read the household transfer slate or question a coachman.

clues.title: A soot-child asks for the white house
clues.description: One dead refugee repeats the direction Judith gave the youngest survivors: “Go to my white house and give the matron your whole name.”
clues.discovery: Open contact with the trapped dead without accepting the Guest in Ash.

clues.title: Mercy House infirmary tags
clues.description: Several bodies carry linen tags from the Mercy House infirmary, including two people still listed publicly as resident patients.
clues.discovery: Examine remains or match tags to the burial roll.

clues.title: Canon Ysra’s sealed inspection request
clues.description: A returned letter requests inspection of the Mercy House upper dormitory after reports of children speaking in absent voices.
clues.discovery: Open the chapel correspondence chest.

clues.title: Every condemned household is inventoried uphill
clues.description: The seizure docket sends beds, tools, winter grain, and children's chests to Blackbriar Hall. The parish storehouse receives only empty tally copies.
clues.discovery: Read the custody column aloud or make Pell explain why parish property never enters parish custody.

clues.title: Quill carries names uphill
clues.description: The familiar’s bone tongue points toward Blackbriar Hall whenever it repeats Judith’s delivery command.
clues.discovery: Capture or kill Quill and examine the bone tongue.

clues.title: A reflected corridor climbs into Blackbriar
clues.description: One reed mirror shows records and captives passing from Saint Mercy House through an upper corridor into Blackbriar Hall's service tunnel.
clues.discovery: Trace the reflected route without stepping into a borrowed image.

clues.title: The service road under the thorns
clues.description: Garran Pike’s wagon road enters a root-cut tunnel beneath the hall rather than approaching its public gates.
clues.discovery: Track the prisoner wagon or force a familiar to reveal its route.

clues.title: Refuge ash seals the oldest pit-dead
clues.description: The first bodies placed in the orchard carry black inward-burning ash in their mouths, and one resistant corpse points west toward Saint Vey's barred granary.
clues.discovery: Examine the earliest trench or free one corpse long enough to indicate its memory.

clues.title: The false shelter ledger
clues.description: Judith’s private ledger lists nineteen refugees as having departed safely, with a separate ash-mark beside each name.
clues.discovery: Search the study or compel a clerk to produce the private volume.

clues.title: Saint Vey granary refugee roll
clues.description: The chapel copy records nineteen people accepted into Judith’s famine shelter and never lawfully released.
clues.discovery: Unwrap the paper around the honest bell’s clapper.

clues.title: Crows roost only west of the burned doors
clues.description: Familiars avoid crossing the original granary threshold and carry ash from its outer bar back to Judith.
clues.discovery: Observe the familiar route or search a captured crow’s feet.

clues.title: Lime wagon ruts leave the refuge road
clues.description: Old wagon grooves run from the burned granary toward the abandoned north orchard, packed with the same quicklime Judith later used to erase the plague dead.
clues.discovery: Clear the ash outside the barred doors or compare the ruts with later corpse-cart tracks.

clues.title: White lime beneath Nell’s feathers
clues.description: Lime tracked into Nell’s room matches the material used in the abandoned orchard trenches and clings to Judith’s crows.
clues.discovery: Examine the sill and compare the substance to local building or burial supplies.

clues.title: Infirmary disposal route
clues.description: The infirmary log sends patients who “failed transfer” to the old north orchard under sealed night orders.
clues.discovery: Read the hidden infirmary book or question Fen Corren.

clues.title: Missing pox procession
clues.description: The chapel chronicle says the pox dead left the village in Judith’s wagons but never arrived at any licensed burial ground.
clues.discovery: Read the pox-year entries and route annotations.

clues.title: Garran’s white-wheeled corpse cart
clues.description: The huntsman’s oldest cart still carries lime in its joints and follows a concealed track to the north orchard.
clues.discovery: Inspect the cart, follow its tracks, or question a prisoner who rode beside it.

clues.title: Caldus remembers which bell made Piers answer himself
clues.description: Brother Caldus says the doorless chapel's small bell once broke Judith's command long enough for Piers Vey to speak his own name. Judith closed the building the next morning.
clues.discovery: Protect Caldus from Cleft and ask what changed between Auda Vey's trial and the chapel closure.

clues.title: Mara’s note: open door, honest bell
clues.description: A margin note directs any surviving investigator to the doorless chapel and warns that its rites require names and witnesses, not faith alone.
clues.discovery: Read Mara’s workroom packet on missing burials.

clues.title: The mere refuses the honest bell's reflection
clues.description: Every copied room appears in the black water except the doorless chapel; when its bell sounds faintly, the nearest stolen reflection returns briefly to its owner.
clues.discovery: Observe the mere while the chapel bell is tested or question the Child about the missing reflection.

clues.title: Nell's drawing of mirrors among reeds
clues.description: Nell drew the mirror dormitory continuing into a black pool where Judith hands paper names to a child-shaped reflection.
clues.discovery: Find the map beneath Nell’s bed.

clues.title: Silver slips wet with mere water
clues.description: The name vessels in the dormitory smell of cold peat and show reed pollen not found near the house.
clues.discovery: Examine a mirror vessel without triggering its inscription.

clues.title: Judith’s moonless appointments
clues.description: A private calendar marks nights without a visible moon and orders a covered carriage to “the glass shore.”
clues.discovery: Read the study calendar or question the night coachman.

clues.title: The naming rite’s warning
clues.description: The counter-rite identifies Moonless Mere as the place where reflections cease belonging to the people who cast them.
clues.discovery: Read the surviving ritual manual.

clues.title: Prison-wagon red leaves the gallows by wing
clues.description: When Judith withdraws, each crow carries a strip cut from the same red cloth used on Garran Pike's covered wagon and flies toward one black line of trees.
clues.discovery: Watch the departure instead of Judith alone, or recover cloth and route strip from a downed bird.

clues.title: The emergency transfer order
clues.description: Sister Harl’s sealed order moves named children through Crow Wood if outsiders enter the upper floors.
clues.discovery: Intercept the order or open the transfer cabinet.

clues.title: Garran’s road allotment
clues.description: Household accounts pay Garran Pike for maintaining a concealed wagon road between Mercy House, the old orchard, and Blackbriar’s undercroft.
clues.discovery: Read the stable accounts or question the hall’s carter.

clues.title: Three chair-signs count down above the undercroft stair
clues.description: Guest, Worm, and Child marks have been cut into the lock plate. A routine Renewal schedule has been struck through and replaced in Judith's hand: midnight tonight, sixty-three copied doors, four places laid, and four living voices required. Beside Canon Ysra's expected arrival date she has written, ‘Join the accounts before they are read.’
clues.discovery: Find the private stair or force Judith, Odo, or Cleft to consult the current feast schedule.

clues.title: Ash doors opening into village hearths
clues.description: When the refuge pact stirs, soot outlines many freestanding doors and all of them lean toward Blackbriar Hill.
clues.discovery: Observe the pact manifestation or question the soot-bound witness.

clues.title: The dead rehearse a supper response
clues.description: Commanded corpses repeat the phrase “Our house receives its mistress” at the same hour each night.
clues.discovery: Listen before disturbing the pits or free one dead enough to answer.

clues.title: Diagram of a many-doored underhall
clues.description: The chapel manual depicts an unlawful feast chamber that joins copied thresholds beneath the host’s own house.
clues.discovery: Reconstruct the damaged counter-rite pages.

clues.title: Prisoners hear the feast below the road
clues.description: Captives in Garran’s wagon hear cutlery and children reciting names beneath the concealed service tunnel.
clues.discovery: Rescue the wagon or enter the tunnel quietly.

clues.title: Judith speaks through a marked guard
clues.description: When challenged, Judith’s voice continues through a guard whose written name she carries, even after she has crossed the green.
clues.discovery: Force her to retreat or disrupt a commanded guard.

clues.title: The witch-poppet is made from Judith's own office
clues.description: Its clove-waxed thread matches Blackbriar supply, and the stuffing is cut from petition forms whose missing corners remain bound in Judith's receipt books.
clues.discovery: Examine thread, wax, paper edge, and filing holes instead of accepting the object as self-proving witchcraft.

clues.title: Altered admissions follow every accusation
clues.description: Mercy House records show Judith admitting or relocating dependents immediately before accusing the adult most likely to object.
clues.discovery: Compare fifteen years of admission and trial dates.

clues.title: Judith’s accusation drafts
clues.description: The study contains prepared confessions and evidence lists for villagers not yet accused, including blank spaces for the triggering incident.
clues.discovery: Search the locked correspondence press.

clues.title: The dead name their jailer
clues.description: The refuge dead remember Judith barring the outer doors and inviting something inside before the flame turned inward.
clues.discovery: Open speech with the trapped dead.

clues.title: Wounds move from Judith into the dead
clues.description: A fresh injury matching harm recently dealt to Judith appears on one unnamed corpse while her own body closes.
clues.discovery: Observe the transfer or compare injuries after confronting her.

clues.title: Her reflection answers before she does
clues.description: Judith’s standing reflection boasts of selecting every “witch” whose death made the village more grateful.
clues.discovery: Question the reflection or force it to replay a naming bargain.

clues.title: Mara’s three-transaction chronology
clues.description: Mara places Judith at the famine fire, pox disappearance, and first name ceremony, with a new class of power appearing after each event.
clues.discovery: Read the hidden board and family packets together.

clues.title: Three chairs in Judith’s private dining room
clues.description: Each chair bears a pact-title and a ledger of payments made after Judith voluntarily renewed its terms.
clues.discovery: Enter the sealed dining room or obtain Judith’s private keys.

clues.title: The Guest remembers her invitation
clues.description: The threshold manifestation repeats Judith’s exact welcome and her promise to provide betrayed shelter in exchange for passage through accepted hearths.
clues.discovery: Witness the pact memory without assenting to it.

clues.title: The Worm’s tally of renewals
clues.description: White worms form dates when Judith returned to offer another unburied body rather than release the original dead.
clues.discovery: Observe the worms under bell sound or controlled light.

clues.title: Judith asked the old priest how to bind three guests
clues.description: The sealed memorandum records her proposed payments in shelter, burial, and names. When the priest called the acts murder and sacrilege, Judith replied that he had confused cost with prohibition.
clues.discovery: Open the confession memorandum with a chapel witness and compare its date with the first new powers.

clues.title: The Child offers Judith’s original bargain
clues.description: The patron’s reflection can replay Judith offering the first seven children’s names in exchange for borrowed voices and command over dreams.
clues.discovery: Refuse the Child’s own bargain and demand a demonstrated memory.

clues.title: The reeve’s token warms when Judith enters
clues.description: Reeve Pell’s blackthorn token heats and the courthouse brazier opens inward when Judith crosses a threshold no one verbally invited her across.
clues.discovery: Notice the token during the confrontation or inspect Pell afterward.

clues.title: The blackthorn horse is addressed to child, mother, and hearth
clues.description: Inside the toy, Nell's whole name is written with Mara's household line and a curl of Sedge ash. The gift records acceptance as a threshold grant rather than affection.
clues.discovery: Open the horse without speaking the inscription near flame or glass.

clues.title: The Mercy Book’s gift column
clues.description: Every magical access incident corresponds to a signed entry recording exactly what the household accepted from Judith.
clues.discovery: Compare the book with resident testimony and village incidents.

clues.title: Ash gallery labels match household tokens
clues.description: Each gallery hearth is labeled with a family signature and fitted with a socket for the matching blackthorn token.
clues.discovery: Enter the ash gallery or study its maintenance diagram.

clues.title: Old hospitality law distinguishes aid from welcome
clues.description: The chapel text warns that a gift accepted under concealed terms does not create moral obligation but can still supply a magical claim until openly revoked.
clues.discovery: Read the threshold doctrine and examples.

clues.title: Reflections enter only marked homes
clues.description: The Child Behind Glass can show many village rooms but fails at households that returned Judith’s gifts or crossed out their signatures.
clues.discovery: Test the reflection network or bargain for a demonstration without giving a name.

clues.title: Crow reports arrive in Judith’s palm
clues.description: A familiar lands without speaking, yet Judith immediately repeats a private sentence uttered at the Sedge Croft.
clues.discovery: Watch her receive Quill or catch the familiar in transit.

clues.title: The hearth mark follows stolen ash
clues.description: The traveling ring contains ash removed from the household’s own fire, linking Judith’s route to a physical sample.
clues.discovery: Analyze the lintel and the unnaturally clean hearth.

clues.title: Mirrors repeat conversations from marked rooms
clues.description: The Glass Nurse echoes words spoken in several homes whose tokens are cataloged in the Mercy Book.
clues.discovery: Listen before the Glass Nurse turns toward the observer, or compare its echoes with household witnesses.

clues.title: The network maintenance board
clues.description: A hall diagram tracks tokens, ash samples, written names, crow routes, and failed household links as separate channels.
clues.discovery: Search the ash gallery workroom.

clues.title: A crow arrives with one strip and one destination
clues.description: Beneath its wing is a folded report naming sender, handoff, and urgency; a thimble of ash hangs separately from the leg. Judith's network travels as cargo, not thought.
clues.discovery: Bring down a messenger without burning or soaking what it carries, then record the intended roost.

clues.title: Nineteen hands knock toward doors, names, and ledger
clues.description: The trapped dead repeat three movements: palms against the outer bar, fingers tracing erased refuge-roll lines, and one hand turning pages that blacken wherever Judith wrote 'departed.'
clues.discovery: Open speech with several refugees and compare the acts they repeat instead of accepting the Guest's explanation.

clues.title: Counter-rite of the freely offered hearth
clues.description: The chapel specifies that the lying shelter record must burn in a hearth freely offered by one Judith betrayed, not in stolen or ownerless flame.
clues.discovery: Repair and read the threshold manual.

clues.title: The private ledger is the pact’s living copy
clues.description: Ash creeps back onto any erased name in Judith’s false shelter ledger, showing that destroying ordinary duplicates will not end the pact.
clues.discovery: Examine the ledger under clean firelight.

clues.title: The Guest recoils from an opened refuge
clues.description: If the three acts are completed, every copied door in the Underhall swings outward and the Guest’s chair cracks; if not, the weak points show what remains undone.
clues.discovery: Observe the pact during the finale or exploit prior partial work.

clues.title: Three pit-dead answer three unfinished duties
clues.description: One scratches at the cut tag, one braces both hands beneath a lime-bound body, and one turns toward every muffled bell stroke. Together they distinguish identification, lifting, and witnessed disposition.
clues.discovery: Give three resistant bodies enough movement or speech to answer separately, then compare their repeated gestures.

clues.title: The honest bell records concealed death
clues.description: The burial rite requires a bell sounded by a witness who states where each body was found and who denied it burial.
clues.discovery: Read the burial office and inspect the bell inscriptions.

clues.title: Infirmary labels restore several identities
clues.description: Patient and transfer records identify eleven of the otherwise erased bodies and connect others to paying households.
clues.discovery: Secure the infirmary records and interview surviving patients.

clues.title: The Worm loses Judith’s wounds when burial begins
clues.description: As named bodies leave the lime under bell sound, injuries stop crossing from Judith into the pits and reappear on her own body.
clues.discovery: Observe the finale after partial or complete burial work.

clues.title: Nell discovers the vessel sequence
clues.description: Nell has learned that a name must be heard in the owner’s own reflection before the mirror is broken; two children injured themselves by reversing the order.
clues.discovery: Question Nell or study the cracked dormitory mirrors.

clues.title: A returned name warms the reflection before the glass
clues.description: When a willing owner speaks their chosen name, their reflection breathes out of time with the patron and moves on its own. A borrowed voice produces a perfect, cold copy.
clues.discovery: Run one controlled return with the vessel covered, the owner consenting, and a free witness ready to stop the sequence.

clues.title: Free-witness clause for missing owners
clues.description: The naming rite permits a free witness who knows the person, relationship, and chosen form of address to return a name when the owner cannot speak.
clues.discovery: Reconstruct the final lines of the naming manual.

clues.title: Judith files wounds by which patron received them
clues.description: Her physician's cabinet separates burns and thresholds, flesh and sickness, recognition and binding. A margin note reads: 'When two fail, the body is merely mine.'
clues.discovery: Compare the three ledgers with injuries witnessed after confronting Judith.

clues.title: Flame takes one kind of harm
clues.description: The Guest in Ash absorbs burns and threshold wounds but cannot mend rot, naming injuries, or ordinary steel once isolated.
clues.discovery: Injure Judith or a pact manifestation while observing the refuge reaction.

clues.title: The pits take flesh wounds
clues.description: Cuts and broken bones migrate to selected corpses, while fire and name-based harms follow different routes.
clues.discovery: Compare Judith’s injuries to the pit dead.

clues.title: Reflections take defeat and recognition
clues.description: The Child can substitute a stolen reflection when Judith is exposed, bound, or struck through her true name, but not after the relevant vessels are returned.
clues.discovery: Test Judith’s reflection or interrogate the patron.

clues.title: Empty chairs remove visible protections
clues.description: Each severed pact leaves one chair empty and strips a distinct set of defenses; with two chairs broken, Judith bleeds and remains where she stands.
clues.discovery: Enter the finale after working against the pact sites.

clues.title: Renewal oath rehearsed at the execution
clues.description: Judith requires the crowd to repeat that every household “receives mercy and its mistress” before accepting new tokens.
clues.discovery: Listen to the formal language or challenge its meaning.

clues.title: Mara’s successful household revocation
clues.description: After Mara withdraws welcome and replaces the stolen ash, Judith cannot cross the croft threshold directly even though the family remains in the Mercy Book.
clues.discovery: Help Mara secure the house or observe Judith’s failed entry.

clues.title: Sister Harl's checklist requires book, hearths, and voices
clues.description: The working list pairs the Mercy Book with displayed household tokens and at least four controlled stolen-name voices. Harl has marked each current child as a consumable placement, not a guest.
clues.discovery: Open the feast cabinet, intercept Harl's transfer copy, or compel her to account for each required placement.

clues.title: Judith’s contingency matrix
clues.description: The final plan states that loss of one component can be absorbed, while loss of any two collapses the common welcome into isolated household claims.
clues.discovery: Search Judith’s study or force her to consult the plan under pressure.

clues.title: Public withdrawal form
clues.description: The chapel records a concise revocation a household can make before witnesses while destroying or returning its token.
clues.discovery: Read the hospitality law and prepare copies for villagers.

clues.title: The rite continues after Judith falls
clues.description: If Judith is killed before two components are removed, the three empty chairs turn toward the Mercy Book and continue the invitation without her.
clues.discovery: Witness the consequence or infer it from the active chamber.

clues.title: Each chair answers a different unfinished duty
clues.description: When the chamber is disturbed, the ash chair closes copied doors, the lime chair pulls wounds into the dead, and the silver chair makes a choir voice answer from the wrong face. The effects remain distinct even when Judith coordinates them.
clues.discovery: Provoke, interrupt, or observe two patron-chair responses and identify the different obligations each one enforces.

clues.title: Copied doors answer only to surviving household carriers
clues.description: The sixty-three copied doors remain dark until matching tokens, signatures, ash packets, gift labels, or custody papers are joined at the token table. A door whose household has revoked its carrier turns outward even while the name remains written in the Mercy Book.
clues.discovery: Compare one active household door with one revoked door while tracing the physical carrier laid into the table.

clues.title: Restored refuge names expose the ash route
clues.description: As the betrayed names return to the refuge roll, soot trails stop vanishing into Judith's general shadow. Each line terminates at a carried ash packet, a marked threshold, or a crow's iron household label; no line crosses open ground without a physical bearer.
clues.discovery: Restore enough names for the dead to distinguish Judith's soot from ordinary fire, then follow one exposed line to its carrier.

clues.title: The mere needs an index before it shows a room
clues.description: A hanging mirror shows only black water until the Glass Nurse presses a written name, token splinter, ash label, or accepted gift against its water knot. Remove the object and the household image collapses instead of following Judith's attention by itself.
clues.discovery: Watch the Glass Nurse prepare a reflected route, or interrupt one and separate the image from the item anchoring it.

clues.title: Auda's last correction names door, roll, and hearth
clues.description: Caldus remembers the three phrases Auda Vey wrote beside Judith's shelter account before the chapel was closed: 'door outward,' 'the names restored,' and 'the lie in a freely offered hearth.' Odo removed the page but copied the charge against Auda into the gallows docket.
clues.discovery: Protect Caldus long enough to reconstruct Auda's suppressed correction and compare it with the charge used to silence her.

clues.title: Caldus's suppressed burial form has three required lines
clues.description: The lawful burial form Judith ordered Caldus to replace has separate spaces for the dead person's identity, the place and manner of recovery, and the witness who sounds the bell at final disposition. Every pox-year substitute leaves all three blank.
clues.discovery: Compare Caldus's retained form with the substituted pox dockets or make Odo explain why the required lines disappeared.

clues.title: Judith's disposal manual marks three failures in red
clues.description: A private disposal manual marks three errors beside transferred wounds: an unnamed body, a body left bound in lime, and a disposition made without the honest bell. Judith's annotations say the Worm retains its claim while any one of the three remains unfinished.
clues.discovery: Search the physician's cabinet or force Odo to produce the instructions used for night removals.

clues.title: The glasswork ledger records what cold breaking steals
clues.description: Three glasswork entries record vessels shattered before the owner's reflection warmed: one child lost speech, one mother ceased recognizing a face, and one captive suffered a matching fracture. A later instruction reads, 'Return the name; wait for warmth; break downward under witness.'
clues.discovery: Read the silverwork account beside the discarded vessel trays or question the servant who cleaned the failed breakages.

clues.title: A returned name loosens the bay before the vessel breaks
clues.description: When a captive speaks their chosen name into an unborrowed reflection, the matching throat wire slackens and the silvered vessel warms before any blow. A cold vessel struck first tightens the choir bay around the owner.
clues.discovery: Attempt one controlled return in the chamber, or compare a warmed vessel with a bay Judith orders broken out of sequence.

clues.title: Two refused debts leave the witch in her own wounds
clues.description: A priest's margin beside the three counter-rites reads: 'One refusal narrows the debt. Two leave the debtor in her own wounds. Three deny the Court succession.' Later hands tested the first sentence and underlined the second.
clues.discovery: Reconstruct the marginal note across the threshold, burial, and naming manuals after repairing the honest bell.

clues.title: The midnight transfer order separates book, carriers, and voices
clues.description: A crow strip assigns three deliveries to different routes: Mercy Book leaves to the undercroft, the token chest to the thorn court, and at least four living named children to the choir bays. Its final line says one missing column can be absorbed; two cannot.
clues.discovery: Capture the three-mark urgency strip before it reaches Garran or compare its route codes with the wagon compartments.

clues.title: The wrong-sky fork ignores an unmarked traveler
clues.description: At one fork, a token-bearing prisoner sees the hall road beneath a wrong noon sky while an unmarked escort sees the ordinary north track. Cover the token or remove the custody paper and both travelers perceive the same path again.
clues.discovery: Separate one active carrier from the person it redirects and compare the route with an unmarked witness.
